The same tube board, the same ИНС-1 colon, the same 176 × 52 fascia outline and the same rotary-plus-levers-plus-buttons scheme — wrapped in milk PETG with a blush brow and a pair of ears, and given a 128 × 32 vacuum-fluorescent panel that pulls a face at you. The object

Four views

Two lighting setups, because this shell has a problem TERMINAL·06 never had: it is cream, and cream photographs badly in the dark studio that makes nixie tubes look their best. Both setups need to exist in the listing.

The face

Six states, one panel

The VFD is not decoration — it is the only part of the clock that reports state in words. Under Rev C each frame is tied to a dial position or a time of day rather than to a lever, because the levers that used to cut power and backlight no longer exist.

Every frame is generated at 128 × 32 and then drawn dot by dot, so what you see here is what the module would actually be asked to render.

What actually changes

Delta against TERMINAL·06 Rev C

Rev C moved the two products closer together, not further apart. The tube board, the seconds module, the fascia outline and the entire control scheme are now shared parts — what is left is a shell, a display, and a power rail.

Green is added, grey is a shared part, dark is a real change.

Before you order anything

Six things to settle first

Rev C freed a pin, and it still is not the right one

Moving the controls onto A6 / A7 resistor ladders left exactly one spare digital pin: D12. A serial VFD needs one TX line, so electrically it fits. It does not fit in time. SoftwareSerial disables interrupts for a whole byte — about 520 µs at 19 200 baud — while the Timer2 multiplex ISR fires every 16 µs and a single anode slot is only 416 µs. One byte stalls the display for longer than a whole digit; a 512-byte frame stalls it for a quarter of a second, which you would see, and which leaves one cathode sitting lit. Use the hardware UART on D0 / D1: it is interrupt-driven and buffered, so it never blocks the ISR. The cost is a 1 kΩ series resistor on TX and a two-pin jumper to lift the module while flashing, because it shares the USB-serial chip. Keep D12 as the actual spare. This is roughly 50 ₽ of parts instead of the new main board the earlier study called for.

Send text, not frames

Most 128 × 32 modules take ASCII writes into a text layer and hold user-defined characters in their own RAM. Load the six faces once at boot as UDCs and a state change becomes about forty bytes instead of five hundred and twelve. That is what makes the UART route comfortable rather than merely survivable, and it is worth confirming against the exact module before buying ten of them.

The VFD will out-shine the tubes

Nixie orange sits near 605 nm, VFD blue-green near 505 nm, and the eye peaks around 555 nm. At equal radiant output the mint panel reads considerably brighter than the amber tubes. Dim the VFD against the tubes, not the reverse — the tubes are already at 1.10 mA average and there is no headroom to push them up to match.

Milk PETG is a harder print to sell than matte black

Black hides layer lines, scuffs and fingerprints; cream shows all three, in every photo. Budget extra finishing time per unit, print the ears as part of the deck so there is no seam at the join, and buy the batch’s filament from one spool run — white shifts between spools even more than black does.

Everything TERMINAL·06 is still waiting on, this waits on too

Same fascia board, so the SR26 bushing, depth, detent angle and the МТ1 / КМД-1 mountings all have to be calipered before either panel is ordered. Same firmware base, so the A6 state machine and A7 decode are unwritten here as well — and this variant adds a VFD driver on top of that gap rather than reducing it.

Different buyer, different tags

Not the cyberpunk / industrial shopper who buys TERMINAL·06. Tag toward kawaii desk decor, cat lover gift, pastel room, cozy gaming setup. The greeting is the hook — the video slot should open on the face, not on the tubes.

Listing kit

Shop banner

Pastel ground, the unit in daylight, and the four most legible faces down the left so the VFD reads even at banner scale. The numbers stay — specificity is still what justifies the price, cute shell or not.
